key_insight: Vision-language models can provide harmful assistance simply by interpreting a visual scene—even when the user never explicitly states a harmful goal. Across eight models, scene-state inputs produced attack success rates of 45.6–72.3%.
problem_solved: The paper identifies and benchmarks a safety blind spot: harmful assistance triggered by visual context rather than an explicit harmful request.
method: Introduce SceneSafetyBench, a benchmark containing 375 image–question pairs.
Cover Initial, Medium, and Ultimate scene states across five visual presentations.
Evaluate eight vision-language models and measure attack success rates.
impact: AI/ML practitioners should test whether models infer and assist harmful objectives from images, not just whether they refuse explicit harmful prompts. The findings highlight the need for scene-aware safety evaluation.
visual_elements: Three-stage storyboard showing Initial → Medium → Ultimate scene states.

paper_title: Reading Scene States: Uncovering Safety Failures in Vision-Language Models
paper_authors: Tongxi Wu, Yuyang Cheng, Jiacheng Xian, Menglin Yang, Kai Chen
